results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 61 body units align one-to-one with spec paragraphs p01-p61 in spec order (verticals p49-p51 after identity, as the revised spec declares); each outliner summary states the aligned paragraph's controlling idea. The five callouts carry no spec paragraph and are listed with matched_spec_paragraph null.

The outliner marked only Introduction ¶1 as having two ideas (prior chapter made listings comparable + where this chapter sits). The spec's p01 controlling idea is exactly that single bridging idea, the chapter's place between normalization and its downstream readers, and the draft states nothing beyond it; its density is recorded under flow_is_followable. No other unit was marked.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: intro and scene to the problem and S1; kinds to S1; identity and verticals to S2; pipeline to S3/S4; merge to S5; practice to S3-S6 (Keybridge p43 to S6, Tradeyard and Barcelona p45-p46 to S1/S4); trade-offs, failure modes, CA view and questions to S4-S6; conclusion to S1/S4/S5.

Every table has a lead sentence that says what it compares (kinds p10, identity p14, verticals p49, merge p32, Lyon listings p38 read by the blocking and scoring paragraphs, trade-offs p47 followed by p48); Figures 1-4 carry captions stating what they show; the Splink, Zillow, OLX, Elastic, PDQ and Idealista sources are each followed by what they show or what they do not; Claire's quotation states the two constraints; the Lyon statistics are interpreted ("which means the removed alerts were noise", "the most valuable labels").

Declared conclusion_summary carrying over 'the stages and the registry' and introducing 'when they run'. The opening sentence starts a new topic and does not gather the stages just described (blocking, scoring, clustering, registry) before saying when they run; coming straight after the registry's lifecycle paragraph, it reads as a return to pipeline mechanics, which both flow readers felt (A6, B6). A sentence that names the stages and the registry as what runs at two speeds would express the summary.

results.quote: This chapter's checks at publication time run inside [[publication-pipeline]], and search, alerts and valuation read the identifiers this chapter gives each cluster, the group of listings that describe one thing.
results.finding: Both flow readers had to re-read the chapter's second sentence: it refers to 'checks at publication time' before any check is described and defines 'cluster' in a trailing appositive that is easy to miss. The spec's p01 order is fine; the sentence packs too much. Split it and define cluster where it is first used.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader A, item A1; flow reader B, item B1

results.finding: Both flow readers felt a step backward: the registry subsection answers Ingrid's third question and moves on to lifecycle and Ghost Inventory, and the pipeline then returns to how fast resolution runs. Both independently propose the same reorder (online-and-batch before or right after clustering, so the registry and its dispute path end the pipeline section and lead into merge policies). The difficulty comes from the declared position of p31 after p29-p30; the spec's flow rationale does not justify that position. Reader A also notes (A7) and reader B also notes (B6) that the answer to the third question has no heading of its own inside 'The entity registry: stable identifiers and lineage'.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader A, items A6 and A7; flow reader B, item B6

Every does_not_know term is given where first used in the body: blocking (p20), pairwise scoring (p22), Fellegi-Sunter (p23), MinHash and SimHash (p20), connected components and chaining (p26), survivorship (p28), field collapsing and its counting limits (p33), T3, DPE and fees-included prices (p06), the Base Adresse Nationale and the RNB (p15). Terms the readers flagged are on already_knows: perceptual hashes (A4/B11; media pipeline) and Common Ground and Motorvane (A13; Veldmark and its brands from earlier chapters). Named people are introduced with their role. Paragraph openings start from introduced material.

The introduction opens with the bridge from normalization and enrichment, then the four-case hook, definitions, scope and a roadmap; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion opens with a synthesis ('Ingrid's four questions turn out to be one'), adds no new subtopic or evidence, does not open with 'in conclusion' and ends on the hand-off to the publication pipeline rather than a restated thesis.

p60 states what no single section states (the four questions reduce to deciding what a duplicate is before how to find it, with kind, entity, registry and policies each setting one part) and why it matters: search, alerts, valuation and pro reporting all count by the cluster identifier, so governing it once lets them agree.
p60 returns to Claire Fontaine's two sentences as callback.to declares: 'It also answers Claire: buyers see the Lyon flat once, and every agency stays one click away under a rule none can buy.'

The cold reader predicted the sections in the order of the spec's roadmap and the actual draft: scene and four questions; kinds; real-world entity by vertical; vertical differences; matching pipeline through stable IDs; registry with dispute path; merge policies with Idealista; Lyon resolved; abuse; trade-offs; failure modes; Chief Architect's view; review questions. It named the evidence (public sources such as Idealista, standards, research, the fictional Veldmark) and the tone. Its splits of the registry and of abuse into their own sections are subsection-level and the roadmap itself groups them ('pipeline and its registry', 'resolved and abuse handled'). The only mismatch with AC-2's expected text is that the expected text lists vertical differences after trade-offs, the older order; the revised roadmap and the draft put it after real-world identity, as the reader predicted.

The reader classed the bike repost as abuse with enforcement owned by trust and safety (with listing policy or monetization), a statement of reasons under DSA Art. 17, original creation date kept and a paid bump offered; the flat as a legitimate multi-agency listing clustered into one canonical property with a stable registry ID, owned by the listing data domain with discovery; and described the buyer view: one card chosen by the published completeness and media-quality rule, 'also listed by 2 other agencies', every agency one click away, leads not re-routed, one alert per property, counts from a property-level index. It does not mention disputes as labels or the published-data-only matcher input, which the probe did not ask about.

The reader named the unstable nightly IDs and the search index as the only record, prescribed an entity registry as system of record with durable IDs, merge and split lineage published as events, reviewer decisions stored as constraints, and counts from a property-level document because collapsing leaves hit counts and aggregations counting listings; all elements of the expected answer.
